world.high_kingdom.desc: A realm beneath the Iron Crown: an oath weighs more than a life, blood comes before merit, and no one beneath the throne truly sleeps.
high_kingdom.npc.1.desc: The white-haired dowager queen, who has spent a lifetime patching the cracks in her son's throne.
high_kingdom.npc.1.l1: The crown has bowed your neck, child — that was never your fault.
high_kingdom.npc.1.l2: Remember: blood is harder to wash out than any oath.
high_kingdom.npc.2.desc: The knight who grew up at your side and now commands the Ironhold guard, his plate polished bright enough to mirror an oath.
high_kingdom.npc.2.l1: Call, and I come — I will not ask why.
high_kingdom.npc.2.l2: Our swords once touched like cups. Do not forget it.
high_kingdom.npc.3.desc: Keeper of the royal library, who knows every coronation and deposition the court has tried to forget.
high_kingdom.npc.3.l1: The old books hold your future; the hand is merely cramped.
high_kingdom.npc.3.l2: The more you learn, the more you must learn to keep silent.
high_kingdom.npc.4.desc: Eldest son of the Duke of the North, whose smile conceals a map of your lands.
high_kingdom.npc.4.l1: The throne answers only to blood, friend. Is yours red enough?
high_kingdom.npc.4.l2: We both know this crown will change heads before long.
high_kingdom.npc.5.desc: The law of the realm made flesh: one word can settle a life, and a loyalty.
high_kingdom.npc.5.l1: The law does not read your heart, only your seal.
high_kingdom.npc.5.l2: Sign it, or burn it — but do not leave it hanging.
high_kingdom.npc.6.desc: Your younger sister, soon to be married across the border to buy a treaty.
high_kingdom.npc.6.l1: Brother, how far away is the place they are sending me?
high_kingdom.npc.6.l2: Don't draw a sword for me. People die when you do.
high_kingdom.npc.7.desc: A knight of no known lineage, called the ghost that betrayed the throne.
high_kingdom.npc.7.l1: The crown is an iron lie. I have worn it.
high_kingdom.npc.8.desc: The royal confessor, who has heard every tear shed upon the throne.
high_kingdom.npc.8.l1: May the light absolve you — and may you see people as they are.
high_kingdom.npc.8.l2: Whatever you confess, I carry it into the grave.
high_kingdom.npc.9.desc: Who taught three generations of the royal line to hold a blade, and now offers you only a word at practice.
high_kingdom.npc.9.l1: A sword is not for winning. It is for living until the moment you must draw.
high_kingdom.npc.9.l2: Your grip is still too eager, my lord.
high_kingdom.npc.10.desc: Keeper of the Great Seal: wherever it falls, there falls the royal command.
high_kingdom.npc.10.l1: The seal knows no man, only the throne.
high_kingdom.npc.10.l2: This decree — will you send it with your blood, or with my wax?
high_kingdom.era.1.desc: The realm was young; the first knightly order broke their blades on the moor and swore an oath never to forswear.
high_kingdom.era.2: The Year of the Anointed Crown
high_kingdom.era.2.desc: The Church crowned the king; the Iron Crown was anointed with oil, and royal power was bound to the will of heaven.
high_kingdom.era.3.desc: Three kings warred without pause; the throne changed masters thrice, and blood reddened the whole Coronation Way.
high_kingdom.era.4.desc: The iron furnaces burned night and day; the realm bought a century of peace with steel — and forged its own chains with it.
high_kingdom.era.5.desc: The Holy See laid excommunication on the realm; throne and altar turned steel on each other, and the bells fell silent for three days.
high_kingdom.era.6.desc: An old king not yet dead, a succession left empty: every ear in the realm is cocked, waiting for one tolling bell.
high_kingdom.fac.1.desc: Forged of iron and oath, and suspended above it, the ambition of every man alive.
high_kingdom.fac.2.desc: The authority of the Church, where absolution and anathema hang on a single breath.
high_kingdom.fac.3.desc: Swords kept in honor's name — who keep their oath, and keep their own fiefs too.
high_kingdom.fac.4.desc: The magnates whose lands are their votes, and whose votes cut deeper than their wars.
high_kingdom.fac.5.desc: The taxpaying hands within the walls: silent, and quietly counting.
high_kingdom.reg.1.desc: The city of the throne: grey stone and high walls, no wind, and no idle talk.
high_kingdom.reg.2.desc: The flagstone road from gate to great hall, worn by every coronation and every bleeding the realm has known.
high_kingdom.reg.3.desc: The sanctuary of the Church; when its bell sounds, the whole city bows its head.
high_kingdom.reg.4.desc: The Duke's frontier, where men in the snow answer to the blade, not to the king.
high_kingdom.reg.5.desc: The realm's granary — and the first place every neighbor's sword is pointed at.
high_kingdom.reg.6.desc: The woodland where the order drills and is knighted, its trunks scarred all over with sword-cuts.
high_kingdom.reg.7.desc: The realm's only harbor, where the customs dues taste as briny as the conspiracies.
high_kingdom.lore.1.body: On the moor the first knightly order broke their own swords over their knees and swore: the blade may break, the oath may not. Ever since, the honor of the realm has hung on that half-length of broken steel.
high_kingdom.lore.2.body: The crown was forged of meteoric iron, and on its inner band is cut a single line — A KING IS ONLY A MAN. At the anointing it lies against the brow, yet no one has ever dared read it aloud.
high_kingdom.lore.3.body: Three kings, three roads of blood, one throne. When the clerks counted the seals after the war, they found the Great Seal had outlived all three of the men who held it.
high_kingdom.lore.4.body: For thirty years the furnaces never went out, and the realm bought peace with steel. Only later did men understand: the iron that makes a sword can also make a chain.
high_kingdom.lore.5.body: The throne does not punish ambition — it merely seats every ambitious man upon the point of a knife.
high_kingdom.lore.6.body: The old scholar said it plainly: a true king does not remember his vassals' names, he remembers what they fear.
high_kingdom.lore.7.body: One pardon is worth a city; the throne's heaviest weight is not its iron but the hand that signs a reprieve.
high_kingdom.lore.8.body: Whoever raises the banner has already forsworn an older oath. Yet sometimes the ones standing beneath it are the farmers the histories forgot.
high_kingdom.lore.9.body: Everyone who has ridden beyond the wall knows: the weeping you cannot hear beneath the throne is perfectly audible at the frontier.
high_kingdom.lore.10: The Crown Grows Into the Skull
high_kingdom.lore.10.body: At sixty you understand: worn long enough, a crown roots into the bone. What keeps it on is not the iron. It is you.
high_kingdom.lore.11.body: A chronicler noted in secret: in the years of fading gold the old king could no longer rise — what sat upon the throne was straw dressed in royal robes.
high_kingdom.lore.12.body: The old king left two wills, one for his son and one for the Church, and at the foot of both was written the same word — empty.
high_kingdom.lore.13.body: At thirty you must choose once between blood and merit; choose wrongly, and the histories will erase the choice for you.
high_kingdom.lore.14.body: At forty-five a king is left with only three kinds of men: those who fear you, those who need you, those who wait for you. Plain speech died with the old ministers.
high_kingdom.lore.15.body: The pardoned traitor did not die; he repaid you by spending his whole life counting your enemies for you.
high_kingdom.lore.16.body: You burned the rebel banner, and the ash blew back onto the battlements — every fleck of it asking: by what right do you sit above?
high_kingdom.fate.1.desc: You will wear it, at the price of seeing only the realm's coat of arms in any mirror, never your own face.
high_kingdom.fate.2.desc: You will be canonized, at the price of having no friend willing to stand beside you while you live.
high_kingdom.fate.3.desc: You will be exiled to the snowbound frontier, where your royal blood is worth less than a knife.
high_kingdom.fate.4.desc: You will lay down your power of your own will, and find that the hand letting go trembles harder than the hand that held.
high_kingdom.fate.5.desc: You will rule the realm for a child, and the realm will remember only the child's name.
high_kingdom.fate.6.desc: You will be the last person to remember the old oath — in an age that no longer needs oaths at all.
high_kingdom.we.1.body: The Iron Crown was dipped in holy oil for the first time; from then on the king's head and the will of heaven were bound together, past all untangling.
high_kingdom.we.2: The War of Three Kings Ends
high_kingdom.we.2.body: When the last king took the throne, the blood of the other two still lay on the Coronation Way; men said three of them had carried the throne up between them.
high_kingdom.we.3.body: The Holy See laid excommunication on the realm, and the bells stopped for three days. In those three days the realm heard its own heartbeat for the first time.
high_kingdom.we.4.body: The Duke of the North refused his tribute, every word of it asking: is a king made by blood, or by the blade?
high_kingdom.we.5.body: The old king of the fading-gold years is dead, his will exists in two copies, the succession lies empty, and the whole city has become a gambling table.
high_kingdom.we.6: The Sacred Crown Is Laid Aside
high_kingdom.we.6.body: The Church drew the holy nail from the crown, and the throne belonged to men alone. The realm breathed out — and then began to be afraid.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.1: A Rider from the March · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.1.text: A mud-caked rider reins in at the gate and demands the king hear him: the Duke of the North has withheld his tribute again, and this time the silver never left the March.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.1.listen.note: You let him speak before the whole hall; the Duke's silence is now an open question.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.1.turn.note: He spits at your feet as he is led away — the March will hear how you treat its messengers.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.2.text: A broker just off the ship offers you a map of the northern coast, and behind it, in a voice for two ears only, word that a foreign crown is courting the Duke.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.2.listen.note: The map is true; you pay in silver and in a favor you may one day regret.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.2.turn.note: He shrugs and sells the map to Lord Reginald, who thanks you for your restraint.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.3: A Barefoot Pilgrim · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.3.text: A pilgrim with bleeding feet sets a sealed letter from the Holy See into your hand and will say only that the bells of the White Tower may soon fall silent.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.3.listen.note: The letter speaks of excommunication if the king does not kneel by spring; the wax smells of Rome.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.3.turn.note: You keep your conscience, and the Holy See keeps a list with your name on it.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.4: A Herald of the Other Claim · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.4.text: A herald in unfamiliar colors walks the Coronation Way reading a proclamation that a distant cousin's claim to the throne is better than the king's.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.4.listen.note: Every word is measured against the silent crowd; half the city leaves wondering, the other half is already counting spears.
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.4.turn: Have him whipped from the city
high_kingdom.ev.stranger.4.turn.note: He is gone by dusk, but the proclamation is memorized by a hundred mouths before the gate closes.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.1.text: In the confusion of unloading, a cask of the year's customs silver is carried off between the crates as if it had never existed.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.1.chase.note: You corner the thieves in a boathouse and take back most of it, at the price of a hand you will never use again.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.1.yield.note: The customs clerks record the loss in silence; the harbor learns that the king's silver can walk.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.2.text: A press of market-goers crowds you at the stalls, and when the crowd thins your purse and your signet seal are gone.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.2.chase.note: You catch a boy with the seal in his fist; he weeps that a man with a red beard paid him for it.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.2.yield.note: The wax is cut anew, and somewhere a forged letter bears the old one.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.3.text: The grain wagons carrying your autumn levy reach Ironhold empty; the drivers swear they were stopped in the night by men in the Duke's colors.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.3.chase.note: You recover the wagons in a barn by the border, but the Duke's men are long gone north.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.3.yield: Feed the city from the reserve
high_kingdom.ev.theft.3.yield.note: The granaries hold; the winter is thinner, and the tenants quietly notice.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.4.text: On the eve of the order's tournament your best plate is stolen from the pavilion; a squire is found asleep at his post, guarding nothing.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.4.chase.note: You find the plate in a charcoal-burner's hut; the man swears a knight in black paid him to carry it.
high_kingdom.ev.theft.4.yield.note: You ride in mismatched plate and lose the first pass badly; the story will outlive the tournament.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.1.text: A sweating sickness spreads through the lower city, and by the third day you are feverish in the keep with the physicians arguing at your door.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.1.nurse.note: You sweat it out over six days and wake thin and grey; the court pretends not to notice what your face now tells.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.1.avoid.note: You escape the fever, and the city notes that the king fled while it died.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.2: Fever in the Snow · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.illness.2.text: Word comes from the March that a garrison of three hundred lies feverish in the cold, and the Duke has not sent so much as a cart of clean water.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.2.nurse.note: Your wagons reach them in time; the survivors will remember which banner fed them.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.2.avoid: Order the Duke to attend them
high_kingdom.ev.illness.2.avoid.note: The Duke answers with a single line — "They are mine to lose" — and the March hears the whole exchange.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.3: The Infirmary at the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.illness.3.text: The abbey infirmary overflows with pilgrims, and the abbess kneels before you to ask for hands, since the sisters can no longer lift them all to their beds.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.3.nurse.note: You carry water through the night; by morning a dying man holds your wrist and calls you by your mother's name.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.3.avoid.note: The abbess thanks you; the sisters do not, and the sick keep dying with their wounds untouched.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.4.text: At harvest the reapers fall sick in the fields, and the reeve begs you either to let the grain stand or feed the men who cannot rise to cut it.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.4.nurse: Feed them, let the grain wait
high_kingdom.ev.illness.4.nurse.note: Half the crop rots in the rain, and no man in Greenvale forgets who chose the people over the sheaves.
high_kingdom.ev.illness.4.avoid.note: The barns fill and the churchyard fills with them together; the valley will speak of this for a generation.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.1.text: The courts uphold your claim to a river-toll long disputed, and the arrears arrive in three carts of silver with the seals still warm.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.1.invest: Rebuild the road and the bridge
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.1.invest.note: The new bridge pays for itself within five years, and the merchants begin to say your name without fear.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.1.save.note: You bank the silver in the keep vault and sleep better than you have in years.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.2.text: The ship you staked in a lean spring returns from the far coast; its hold is heavy with spice and its captain is grinning.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.2.invest.note: The second ship does as well as the first, and you begin to think of a fleet.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.2.save.note: The money is safe, and your name upon the harbor is that of a cautious man.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.3.text: The summer is kind and the valley yields twice an ordinary crop; the reeve asks what to do with more grain than the barns can hold.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.3.invest: Sell south before the price falls
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.3.invest.note: Your agents sell early and well; the brokers curse you and the treasury blesses you.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.3.save.note: The surplus is stored against famine; a year later, that decision feeds a whole city.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.4: The Tourney Purse · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.4.text: You unhorse three knights at the order's tournament and take the champion's purse, to the visible displeasure of Lord Reginald in the stands.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.4.invest.note: You buy horses and goodwill with the winnings; two of the knights you felled will now serve you gladly.
high_kingdom.ev.windfall.4.save.note: The purse goes into the treasury, and Reginald smiles thinly as if you had taken something of his.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.1.text: Your steward has been selling the keep's grain stores to your rival for years, and the ledger he kept to cover it was found in the seam of his coat.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.1.confront.note: He breaks and weeps before the court, naming debts and a sister held hostage; but the damage is already north.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.1.plan.note: You let him think himself safe, and use him to feed false figures to your rival all winter.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.2: A Claimed Deed · the Lords' Council
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.2.text: At the council Lord Reginald rises and claims as his own the deed you won at Saltport, with a witness you recognize as your former clerk.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.2.confront.note: Your clerk cannot look at you; the council sees his eyes drop, and Reginald loses the day — for now.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.2.plan.note: You let Reginald think he has won, and begin quietly to buy the debts of every lord who stood at his shoulder.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.3: A Knight Defects · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.3.text: Sir Bran, sworn to your household for a decade, rides out in the grey before dawn and is seen next at the Black Knight Mordred's side.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.3.confront.note: You catch him at the ford; he will not meet your eye, and the words exchanged there neither of you ever repeat.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.3.plan.note: You provide for his wife and children with perfect courtesy, and let the whole realm watch him be shamed by your kindness.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.4.text: Your customs agent at Saltport has been skimmed the king's tariffs into his own strongbox; a curious clerk with an honest streak has brought you the tally.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.4.confront.note: He is taken with the coin still on him; the harbor watches, and the other agents become suddenly, tremblingly precise.
high_kingdom.ev.betrayal.4.plan.note: You let him run, charting every name he pays, until the whole smuggling ring stands exposed in the palm of your hand.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.1.text: The anniversary of the anointing fills Ironhold with banners and wine; every lord and every grievance in the realm attends the same long table.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.1.join.note: You drink with the realm and hear three confessions you were never meant to hear; the wine is worth the headache.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.1.work: Keep the table small and the doors watched
high_kingdom.ev.festival.1.work.note: The feast is orderly, dull, and safe — and every guest notices that the king did not sit among them.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.2.text: The tenants of Greenvale kindle their lanterns for harvest home and send word that they will wait until their lord comes to cut the first sheaf.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.2.join.note: You swing the sickle with borrowed arms before a cheering valley; the tenants will tell their grandchildren.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.2.work: Send the steward in your place
high_kingdom.ev.festival.2.work.note: The feast goes on without you; the songs are a little quieter, and the reeve does not mention your name.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.3: The Order's Muster · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.festival.3.text: The knightly order gathers in the wood for its yearly muster, mass, and tournament, and by custom the throne must bless the new blades.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.3.join.note: You take the vigil and the anointing on one knee; three young men will carry that memory into every battle.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.3.work: Send your marshal to bless them
high_kingdom.ev.festival.3.work.note: The ceremony proceeds; the order accepts your proxy and remembers, privately, that you were absent.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.4: The Vigil of the Nail · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.festival.4.text: On the night the Church keeps the vigil of the holy nail, the White Tower invites you to keep the watch in the crypt with the reliquary.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.4.join.note: You kneel in the cold stone all night, and come out with something in your face the bishops will remember.
high_kingdom.ev.festival.4.work: Send a chaplain with a gift
high_kingdom.ev.festival.4.work.note: The gold is accepted; the vigil is kept without you, and the Church marks the difference between a gift and a presence.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.1: The Whisper in the Guardroom · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.1.text: Your own guards are saying the old king has been dead for a season and the throne sits above a covered corpse.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.1.trace: Trace the first man who said it
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.1.trace.note: It began with a physician's servant from the palace; the trail leads uncomfortably close to your own household.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.1.ignore.note: The whisper spreads from the guardroom to the market; silence is taken for proof.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.2: A Song at the Fair · Saltport
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.2.text: At the harbor fair a ballad is sung in which a greedy lord taxes the poor to gild his own banner — and the lord has your face.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.2.trace: Find the man who wrote it
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.2.trace.note: You find a half-blind former soldier whose village you once burned; you listen to him, and pay him, and neither of you sleeps well.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.2.ignore.note: The song spreads; by winter it is sung in three cities, each verse a little crueler.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.3: A Letter Intercepted · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.3.text: A courier is stopped on the Coronation Way carrying a letter that names you as the next head to roll when the Duke comes south.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.3.trace.note: You follow him to a country inn where the Duke's agents meet monthly; what you learn there changes your winter plans.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.3.ignore.note: You let it go and set a watcher on the man it is meant for; patience may yet buy you the whole net.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.4: A Sermon from the Pulpit · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.4.text: A priest at the White Tower preaches that a realm ruled by an unrepentant king is a realm already under judgment.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.4.trace: Ask the bishop who wrote the text
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.4.trace.note: The bishop folds his hands and names a cardinal in Rome — and asks, with perfect mildness, what you intend to do about it.
high_kingdom.ev.rumor.4.ignore.note: The congregation files out in silence; half of them begin to believe it.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.1: The Road to the March · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.journey.1.text: A summons from the Duke requires you to ride into the snowbound March in person, where the greeting is as likely to be a knife as a horn of mead.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.1.go.note: You see with your own eyes how thin the Duke's loyalty has worn; the snow keeps no secrets.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.1.stay.note: Your envoy returns with the Duke's contempt written plainly in the price he set for obedience.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.2: The Pilgrim Road · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.journey.2.text: The Church asks you to escort a relic on pilgrimage down the Coronation Way, a procession of three days through the realm's most devout towns.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.2.go.note: You walk barefoot the last mile with the pilgrims; the Church's scribes write your name in gold, and the common folk remember your blistered feet.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.2.stay.note: The relic travels safely; the pilgrims notice that the throne sent soldiers, not a lord.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.3: A Summons Across the Sea · Saltport
high_kingdom.ev.journey.3.text: A ship waits at Saltport with a letter from a foreign crown offering terms of marriage and alliance, if you will come in person to treat.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.3.go.note: You treat with a foreign court and return with a treaty and a cold, beautiful memory of what you almost became.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.3.stay.note: The letters go back and forth all year; the marriage is arranged for your sister instead, and you sign it in your own hall.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.4.text: Custom demands the king hold winter court in Greenvale, hearing petitions from the whole middle realm where the roads meet.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.4.go.note: You sit in the draughty hall for a week and settle a hundred quarrels; two of them will make war if you do not return next year.
high_kingdom.ev.journey.4.stay.note: The reeve rules well in your name and quietly becomes the most important man in the valley.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.1: A Challenge at the Table · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.duel.1.text: At the feast, Lord Reginald lays his glove on the board and says that a certain man's honor has been long overdue an answer.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.1.fight.note: You meet in the yard at dawn; neither of you kills the other, and both of you learn the other's measure.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.1.decline.note: The hall falls silent; Reginald smiles as though you have confirmed something he already believed.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.2: A Knight's Charge · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.duel.2.text: A young knight of the order accuses you before the assembled brothers of breaking the oath of the wood in a border skirmish.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.2.fight.note: You fight under the trees where the oath was sworn; the order judges the outcome and finds, narrowly, for your truth.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.2.decline.note: You bow your head to the brothers' verdict; some call it humility, others weakness, and the order is never quite sure which.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.3: A Challenge in the Snow · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.duel.3.text: A champion in the Duke's colors rides to the ford and calls for any man of the king's to dispute the North's right to its own tolls.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.3.fight.note: You unhorse him at the third pass; the North's champion yields, and the Duke watches from the ridge saying nothing.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.3.decline.note: Your refusal is read as fear; the North doubles its tolls the next week and no one stops them.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4: A Poet's Insult · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4.text: A court poet, safe behind his patron's name, composes a verse implying that your father's blood may not have been his own.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4.fight: Name him a liar to his face
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4.fight.note: The poet pales and recants; his patron takes the insult personally and begins to collect your enemies.
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4.decline: Answer with a feast and a pension
high_kingdom.ev.duel.4.decline.note: You feed the poet at your own table until his verses turn kind; the realm finds the whole thing faintly ridiculous, which is exactly what you wanted.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.1.text: The valley yields barely half a crop, and the reeve asks whether the levy should be taken in full from tenants who will not have seed corn for spring.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.1.share: Halve the levy and open the granary
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.1.share.note: You feed the valley through winter and enter spring with its love, its seed, and an empty treasury.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.1.hoard.note: The barns are full and the churchyard fills with the thin; the spring planting is done by fewer hands.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.2: A Raided Field · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.2.text: The Duke's riders swept through the border farms and took a full season's grain as "tribute due in arrears".
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.2.share.note: The border farms survive on your grain; the Duke's hold on them loosens by a night's ride, to the width of a loyal road.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.2.hoard: Tell them to petition the Duke
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.2.hoard.note: The farms petition; the Duke laughs and takes the oxen too.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.3.text: A merchant offers you a hold of southern wheat at a ruinous price, knowing the city will starve without it and that you know it too.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.3.share: Buy it and sell it cheap
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.3.share.note: The city eats and the treasury bleeds; the guilds speak of you with the particular warmth of men who have been saved a fortune.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.3.hoard: Buy it and sell it dear
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.3.hoard.note: You make a killing and are cursed in every bread queue; the coins gleam, and the names stick.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.4: The Order's Tithe · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.4.text: The knightly order demands a larger share of the valley's harvest as tithe, citing the cost of defending a realm whose king will not pay.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.4.share.note: The order is funded, the roads are safe, and the valley's tenants pay for all of it with a mutter.
high_kingdom.ev.harvest.4.hoard.note: You keep the grain; the order's patrols thin, and by autumn the roads out of Greenvale are no longer safe after dark.
high_kingdom.ev.law.1.text: Chief Justice Cedric brings an edict requiring every lord to renew his seal before the throne, or forfeit his lands.
high_kingdom.ev.law.1.obey.note: You kneel and set your seal in the Great Register; the other lords watch, and several discover urgent business elsewhere.
high_kingdom.ev.law.1.defy.note: You refuse on ancient precedent; the Justice records your refusal without expression, which is worse than argument.
high_kingdom.ev.law.2.text: A yeoman hanged for poaching on your own land has left a widow who claims the death was unlawful, since the wood had been common ground for a century.
high_kingdom.ev.law.2.obey.note: The widow is turned away; the commoners of Greenvale mark that the king's law is the lord's convenience by another name.
high_kingdom.ev.law.2.defy.note: You sit as judge over your own reeve and find in the widow's favor; the reeve resigns, and the valley believes, cautiously, in your justice.
high_kingdom.ev.law.3: The Church's Court · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.law.3.text: A priest accused of murder claims benefit of clergy, demanding to be tried by the bishop rather than by the king's law.
high_kingdom.ev.law.3.obey.note: The bishop tries him and lets him retire to a monastery; the realm learns that a clerk may kill without paying.
high_kingdom.ev.law.3.defy.note: You take him from the sanctuary gates; the Church pronounces censure, and the bells of the White Tower ring a knell at your name.
high_kingdom.ev.law.4.text: The throne — or its clerks, on the throne's behalf — levies a new tax on exported wool, without the council's consent.
high_kingdom.ev.law.4.obey.note: The tax is gathered and the guildmasters swallow it, memorizing the date.
high_kingdom.ev.law.4.defy.note: You refuse, and the boldness of it becomes the first sentence in every later argument about who truly rules.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.1: The Duke's Daughter · the Lords' Council
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.1.text: At the council you meet the Duke of the North's daughter, sharp-eyed and unhappily betrothed elsewhere, and find yourself lingering in doorways.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.1.woo.note: You court her in full view of the realm; the Duke calls it war, the Church calls it tangled, and she calls it, smiling, late.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.1.friend.note: You become the one person she tells the truth; it will cost you both more than a courtship ever would, and last far longer.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.2: A Healer's Hands · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.2.text: A young healer at the abbey mends your wound after a skirmish and tells you, quite calmly, that you will die young if you keep riding at the front.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.2.woo.note: You find reasons to be wounded; she sees through every one of them and refuses to mind.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.2.friend: Ask her to be your physician
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.2.friend.note: She becomes the only person in the realm permitted to tell you an unwelcome truth, and tells you several.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3: A Song in the Hall · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3.text: A minstrel in the palace hall sings a song you have heard a hundred times before, and this time you cannot take your eyes off him.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3.woo: Ask him to stay past winter
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3.woo.note: He stays, and his songs grow pointed and political, and you find that love and danger have begun to share a bed.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3.friend: Commission him a song of your own
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.3.friend.note: He writes you a song about a lonely throne, and it is the truest portrait of you that anyone has ever made.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.4: A Rival's Sister · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.4.text: The sister of the man you are feuding with arrives at the wood to plead for his life, and is nothing like the man she pleads for.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.4.woo.note: The feud becomes intolerable; the realm whispers of an alliance bought with a bed, and she hears every whisper.
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.4.friend: Help her, and keep your distance
high_kingdom.ev.first_love.4.friend.note: You grant her plea and keep your word; years later, when her brother betrays you both, she is the one who sends warning.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.1: A Knight Falls · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.grief.1.text: Sir Bran, your oldest companion, is carried back from the border skirmish with the Duke's riders, dead before the surgeons can unpack their knives.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.1.mourn.note: You keep vigil three nights and weep only once, at the very end, when no one else is in the chapel.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.1.carry.note: You bury him by the ford and go straight back to the war; the men follow you, and study your face when they think you are not looking.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.2.text: The queen, long ill, dies at the turning of the year, and the realm expects a king's mourning in full and public measure.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.2.mourn: Mourn in the hall before all
high_kingdom.ev.grief.2.mourn.note: You let the realm see your grief; it makes you human to the commons and mortal to your rivals.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.2.carry: Mourn alone, rule in the morning
high_kingdom.ev.grief.2.carry.note: You govern as though nothing had happened; the court calls it strength, and only the servants in the corridor know otherwise.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3: The Children of the Fever · Greenvale
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3.text: The blight-fever carries off forty of the valley's children in a fortnight, and the reeve sends you the list, written in a careful, shaking hand.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3.mourn: Ride down and read the names aloud
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3.mourn.note: You read every name at the grave-pit and stand in the rain until the last is spoken; the valley will never fully hate you again.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3.carry: Order a chapel built in their memory
high_kingdom.ev.grief.3.carry.note: The chapel rises stone by stone; the masons carve no names, only an empty arch, and the mothers find that worse.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.4: A Confessor's End · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.grief.4.text: Old Father Bernard, who heard every confession the throne has carried for thirty years, dies in his cell with a locked box beside him.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.4.mourn.note: You sit with the old man a last hour and cannot bring yourself to touch the box, which is another kind of grief.
high_kingdom.ev.grief.4.carry: Take the box and open it
high_kingdom.ev.grief.4.carry.note: The box holds decades of written confessions; you burn them unread at the altar, and the smoke smells of a whole generation's secrets.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.1.text: A master armorer offers to take you as a pupil for one winter, saying your grip is wasted on a king and made for a forge.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.1.take.note: You spend a winter at the anvil and forge a blade with your own hands; it is crooked, and you carry it always.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.1.refuse.note: You pay for the next generation of armorers; the master calls you a fool with a good checkbook, and forgives you in a year.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.2: The Falconer's Art · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.craft.2.text: An old falconer in the wood, keeper of the realm's hawks, offers to teach you the patience of training a bird that will never love you.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.2.take.note: You learn that command is a matter of patience and hunger; it changes how you rule, and how you wait.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.2.refuse: Let the falconer keep his art
high_kingdom.ev.craft.2.refuse.note: The old man keeps his birds and his solitude; the realm loses nothing it can name, and you lose something you cannot.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.3: A Stonemason's Offer · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.craft.3.text: The mason rebuilding the Coronation Way offers to let you set the first stone yourself, so that the road carries your hand as well as your name.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.3.take.note: Your hands are in the mortar that will outlast you; the masons cheer, and you never again pass the road without looking down.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.3.refuse: Leave it to the guild alone
high_kingdom.ev.craft.3.refuse.note: The guild builds the road without you; it is done well, and your absence is carved nowhere, which is how you preferred it.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.4.text: Old Scholar Alwyn offers to teach you the scribe's hand, saying a king who cannot write his own decrees will always be ruled by whoever can.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.4.take.note: You learn, badly and then well; the first decree you write yourself is a pardon, and no one can prove it was not the clerk's.
high_kingdom.ev.craft.4.refuse.note: You rule by seal and clerk as your fathers did; Alwyn says nothing, which from him is a very long remark.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.1: A Second Will · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.secret.1.text: A frightened clerk confesses that two wills exist under the old king's seal, one for the heir and one for the Church, and that they do not agree.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.1.open.note: The wills are read before the council; the realm learns that its future was left deliberately open, and the council splits in an hour.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.1.leave.note: The second will goes into a vault only three men know of; you sleep as well as any of them, and no better.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.2.text: Father Bernard, on his deathbed, tells you that your own father died by no natural means, and that the hand was one you have dined with.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.2.open.note: You pull the thread through years of court history; what you find does not make you freer, only older.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.2.leave: Let the old man take it to the grave
high_kingdom.ev.secret.2.leave.note: You close the cell door behind you and never speak of it; the man in question dies peacefully, unknowing, many years later.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.3: A Bastard's Claim · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.secret.3.text: A hedge knight in the March claims to be the old king's unacknowledged son, and has the look of the royal line about him.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.3.open: Bring him to court and settle it
high_kingdom.ev.secret.3.open.note: You bring him south and let the Church decide; he is declared false, and the look of the royal line is never explained.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.3.leave.note: He takes the gold and goes quiet; years later a man with the same face commands a company on the wrong side of a border.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.4.text: A customs clerk offers you a ledger showing which lords of the realm have been borrowing from a foreign power, and on what terms.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.4.open.note: You summon them one by one; three confess, one flees, and the realm learns that the throne can read its debts.
high_kingdom.ev.secret.4.leave: Keep the ledger secret and useful
high_kingdom.ev.secret.4.leave.note: The ledger becomes a shelf of quiet leverage; every lord in it behaves impeccably, and knows exactly why.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.1.text: No rain falls from spring to harvest, the wells sink to mud, and the reeve asks whether the river-water is to go to the fields or the city.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.1.ration.note: Every field gets a little and no field gets enough; the valley survives on the edge, tired but alive.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.1.take: Take the water for the city
high_kingdom.ev.drought.1.take.note: Ironhold drinks and Greenvale withers; the valley sends no grain, and no petition, only silence.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.2: The White Tower's Wells · the Capital
high_kingdom.ev.drought.2.text: The abbey's ancient wells run dry, and the Church asks you to open the royal cistern to the poor who have come to the walls for water.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.2.ration.note: The poor drink by turns with the garrison; the arrangement breeds quarrels but no deaths, and the Church notes your fairness.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.2.take: Close the cistern to the realm
high_kingdom.ev.drought.2.take.note: You keep the water for the keep; the Church calls the thirst a judgment, and the poor remember who held the key.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3: Cattle Die on the March · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3.text: The Duke's herds, and the border farms', are dying by the score, and the Duke asks whether the crown will send water-carts south of the line.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3.ration: Send what water you can spare
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3.ration.note: The carts go north with guards and leave half the herds alive; the Duke's grudge softens by exactly the width of the favor.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3.take: Hold your water behind the border
high_kingdom.ev.drought.3.take.note: The herds die; the border farms learn that the crown's mercy stops at the frontier post.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.4: A Pilgrim's Drought · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.drought.4.text: A preacher declares the drought a punishment for the realm's sins and calls on the king to walk barefoot and beg the rain.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.4.ration.note: You walk with the pilgrims and fast three days; the rain comes, or the season changes, and no one can tell which.
high_kingdom.ev.drought.4.take: Dismiss the preacher as a rabble-rouser
high_kingdom.ev.drought.4.take.note: He is silenced; the drought ends on its own, and the realm remembers that the king did not kneel.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.1: A Ring from the Duke · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.gift.1.text: The Duke of the North sends you a heavy silver ring by a rider who says, smiling, that it is the Duke's own, worn at his own wedding.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.1.accept.note: You wear it openly; the court reads it as a bond, and the Duke, hearing of it, sends you an even warmer letter.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.1.suspect: Have it examined by a goldsmith
high_kingdom.ev.gift.1.suspect.note: The goldsmith finds a hollow in the band, and inside it, a scrap of paper with a name that is not the Duke's.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.2: A Relic from the Church · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.gift.2.text: The Church offers you a reliquary said to hold a finger-bone of the saint whose nail crowns the realm, as a token of favor.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.2.accept.note: You receive it publicly and build it an altar; the Church is pleased, and the relic conveniently never performs a miracle you must explain.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.2.suspect: Ask the physicians to examine it
high_kingdom.ev.gift.2.suspect.note: The bone turns out to belong to a large bird; the Church is embarrassed, and you are now the man who questioned a holy thing.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.3: A Horse from the Duke's Heir · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.gift.3.text: Reginald, the Duke's heir, gives you a black stallion on the morning of the tournament, saying it is the fastest in the North.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.3.accept.note: You ride the stallion and it nearly throws you at the third tilt; you win anyway, and Reginald's smile never wavers.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.3.suspect: Have the groom watch it at night
high_kingdom.ev.gift.3.suspect.note: The groom catches a boy with a burr under the saddle; the boy names no one, and Reginald is most sympathetic.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.4: A Chest from a Merchant · Saltport
high_kingdom.ev.gift.4.text: A merchant whose life you once spared sends a chest of southern silk and a note saying only that a debt is a debt.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.4.accept: Keep the silk and send thanks
high_kingdom.ev.gift.4.accept.note: You wear the silk at the winter feast and the merchant's name spreads among the guilds as the king's friend.
high_kingdom.ev.gift.4.suspect.note: The chest goes back; the merchant never writes again, and you never learn what the note under the silk said.
high_kingdom.ev.war.1: A Summons to the Field · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.war.1.text: The Duke of the North has crossed the ford with his riders, and the marshal asks whether the crown will meet him in the field or behind walls.
high_kingdom.ev.war.1.serve.note: You ride at the head of the levy and are seen by every soldier; whatever comes next, no one can say the king stayed home.
high_kingdom.ev.war.1.hide.note: You yield the open country and save your strength; the North burns three valleys, and the rhyme about the hiding king is written by autumn.
high_kingdom.ev.war.2: A War of the Church · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.war.2.text: The Holy See declares a crusade against a heretic neighbor and calls upon the realm's knights to take the cross.
high_kingdom.ev.war.2.serve: Send the order and take the cross
high_kingdom.ev.war.2.serve.note: Your knights ride out beneath two banners; some return changed, some return rich, and some do not return.
high_kingdom.ev.war.2.hide.note: The order obeys the throne and disobeys its faith; the Church marks the realm as lukewarm, and the knights mark you as their chain.
high_kingdom.ev.war.3.text: Two allied trading cities begin a war that will close the sea-lanes, and each asks the realm to take its side.
high_kingdom.ev.war.3.serve.note: You send ships and lose two; the surviving captains come home with plunder and a lasting grudge against you for the two.
high_kingdom.ev.war.3.hide.note: Both cities curse you and both keep trading; your customs revenue triples, and your honor is quietly priced accordingly.
high_kingdom.ev.war.4: The Levy of the Valley · Greenvale
high_kingdom.ev.war.4.text: The marshal calls the valley's men to the levy, and the reeve warns that taking them will leave the harvest to the old and the very young.
high_kingdom.ev.war.4.serve.note: The valley sends its sons; two of them come back, and the harvest comes in thin and late.
high_kingdom.ev.war.4.hide.note: The other lords notice the hole in your levy and fill it with their talk; your fields are fat and your honor thinner.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.1.text: A hard winter empties the city's bread queues, and a crowd gathers below the keep shouting that the throne eats while the realm starves.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.1.share.note: The bread comes out by the cartload and the crowd disperses; the treasury takes the loss, and the city's mood eases for a season.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.1.close: Bar the gates and hold the grain
high_kingdom.ev.famine.1.close.note: The guards hold the square; the hunger does not, and the city learns exactly how much its king is willing to spend on it.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.2.text: Greenvale sends its reeve to beg for seed corn, having eaten next year's planting to survive this year's hunger.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.2.share: Send seed and forgive the levy
high_kingdom.ev.famine.2.share.note: You send the corn; the valley plants a spring you will not see taxed for three years, and remembers.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.2.close: Send nothing; collect the levy later
high_kingdom.ev.famine.2.close.note: The valley eats its seed and cannot plant; the levy of the following years shrinks to almost nothing, and so does the valley.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.3: The Church's Barns · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.famine.3.text: The Church holds full barns while the poor die at its walls, and the bishop offers to open them only if the crown will match the gift.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.3.share.note: The two granaries open together; the poor are fed, and the bishop's reputation grows at the same rate as your expense.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.3.close.note: The barns stay shut; the bishop preaches on the sin of a sealed granary, and the realm takes his meaning.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.4.text: Word reaches you that certain guildmasters are hoarding grain against the price, buying famine on purpose to sell it back dear.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.4.share: Seize the hoards and sell cheap
high_kingdom.ev.famine.4.share.note: The hoards are opened in the market square; the guildmasters are ruined, and the merchants of Saltport never quite trust the throne again.
high_kingdom.ev.famine.4.close: Buy their grain at their price
high_kingdom.ev.famine.4.close.note: You pay the famine price and feed the city; the guildmasters grow rich, and the city does not learn where its bread came from.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.1.text: The ancient rite requires the king to spend the eve of his crowning alone in the crypt, keeping watch over his ancestors' bones.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.1.keep: Keep the watch in the crypt
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.1.keep.note: You kneel all night among the stone kings; what you meet there you never describe to anyone.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.1.break.note: You are crowned in the morning without the night; the old lords say nothing, and every one of them remembers the omission.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.2: The Oath of the Wood · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.2.text: The order asks you to renew, in person, the ancient oath sworn in the wood — the same oath your grandfather broke.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.2.keep.note: You swear the old words your grandfather forswore; the trees are silent, and the knights are not.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.2.break: Rewrite the oath to the throne's use
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.2.break.note: You rewrite the words to bind the order closer to the crown; the older knights see the change and never forgive it.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.3.text: The valley keeps an old feast on the day the realm's histories say nothing happened, and the reeve invites you to abolish it as idle and superstitious.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.3.keep: Attend the feast and let it stand
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.3.keep.note: You sit through the strange old songs; no one can explain them to you, and the valley is quietly, deeply glad you came.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.3.break.note: The feast is cancelled; the valley obeys, and the songs move underground, where they grow sharper.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.4: The Trial of the Blade · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.4.text: By tradition a new king must, on the Coronation Way, strike a ceremonial blow against a shield hung at the gate, to show his arm is still a man's.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.4.keep.note: You strike it once, hard, and the dent remains in the shield for a generation of kings to match.
high_kingdom.ev.tradition.4.break.note: You walk past the shield and into your hall; the commons, who had come to see the blow, go home telling a smaller story.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.1.text: The realm's chief chronicler asks to record your reign as you wish it remembered, with all the drafts under your seal.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.1.write.note: You give the chronicler the reign you meant to have; the realm will read a cleaner king than it lived under, and you know it.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.1.silent.note: You let the chronicler write only what he witnessed; he records small things, and the portrait is truer and colder than any you would have chosen.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.2: A Bastard Child · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.2.text: A woman from the border brings you a child she says is your father's, and asks only that the child not inherit poverty with your face.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.2.write.note: You set the child's name in the register and give it lands; the court mutters about the line of succession, and the child grows up courted for its claim.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.2.silent.note: The child is fed and schooled and never knows why; you watch it grow from a distance, and it grows up hating a king it cannot name.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.3: A Dying Lord's Question · the Lords' Council
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.3.text: An old lord on his deathbed asks you what you intend to leave behind, having spent his own life acquiring lands he now cannot take with him.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.3.write: Answer him with a plan for the realm
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.3.write.note: You tell him of walls and laws meant to outlast you; he says it is the answer of a young man, and dies content anyway.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.3.silent.note: You sit with him and say nothing certain; he laughs, calls it the only honest answer in the court, and dies holding your hand.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4: The Founder's Tomb · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4.text: The tomb of the realm's founder is to be opened for repairs, and custom says the king must be present when the first stone is lifted.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4.write: Attend and record what is found
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4.write.note: The tomb holds less than the legends promised; you record the truth, and the realm's founding grows smaller and truer in the same gesture.
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4.silent: Seal the tomb and the account
high_kingdom.ev.legacy.4.silent.note: You seal the tomb and forbid the record; the legends hold, and so does the small truth, buried with them.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.1: The Duke's Offer · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.1.text: The Duke of the North offers you a partition of the realm: he keeps the North in full, you keep the South, and together you set aside the old succession.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.1.resist.note: You refuse the offer and send the letter to the council; the Duke is shamed, and you now have an enemy who knows your price is not silver.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.1.yield.note: You agree in a room with two candles and one witness; from that night the realm is one house with two roofs, and you are never again able to sleep through an unexpected knock.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.2.text: A quiet man in the keep offers to remove Lord Reginald for the price of a single sentence never spoken aloud.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.2.resist.note: You send the poisoner away and warn your rival, who is baffled and then, unwillingly, grateful.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.2.yield.note: You say nothing, and Reginald takes to his bed by the new moon; no one accuses you, and no one ever quite stops.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.3.text: A foreign crown offers you a fortune in gold to look aside while its ships use your harbor to move troops against a neighbor.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.3.resist.note: The ships are turned away; the foreign crown's envoys call you a fool, and your neighbors, hearing it, become a little safer to trade with.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.3.yield: Take the gold and look aside
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.3.yield.note: The gold buys you a fleet; the neighbor learns where the troops landed from, and the next war begins with your name in its first line.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.4: An Outlawed Brother's Plea · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.4.text: Your own brother, outlawed years ago for a killing he swears was justice, asks to be taken back into the line of inheritance.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.4.resist.note: You refuse and offer him a distant command instead; he accepts, and serves you loyally, and never speaks of it.
high_kingdom.ev.temptation.4.yield.note: You restore him and the court divides neatly in two; the smaller half becomes your brother's, and the larger keeps counting.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.1.text: Raiders from across the border have fired a village in the valley, and its people are trapped between the flames and the river.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.1.help.note: You pull people from the water with your own hands; three of them live because of it, and the valley tells the story for decades.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.1.pass: Wait for the raid to run its course
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.1.pass.note: The raiders take what they came for and leave; the survivors count the dead, and count also which banner did not appear.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.2: A Ship in the Storm · Saltport
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.2.text: A ship breaks its moorings in the harbor storm with a full crew aboard, and the harbormaster says no boat can reach it.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.2.help.note: You go out in the second boat and lose two men and save nine; the harbor will argue forever whether it was courage or folly.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.2.pass: Forbid any boat to go out
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.2.pass.note: The ship breaks on the mole and the crew with it; no one blames you, and the harbor is never quite warm to you again.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3: A Hostage in the March · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3.text: The Duke has taken a lord's son hostage against a debt, and the lord asks you to ransom the boy before winter takes him.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3.help: Pay the ransom from the treasury
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3.help.note: The boy comes home thin and silent; the lord becomes your man body and soul, and the Duke sells you nothing else that year.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3.pass: Let the lord ransom his own
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.3.pass.note: The lord cannot raise it; the boy dies in the March, and his father will remember at every council which way the king voted.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.4.text: The whole city watches as fire takes a poor quarter, and the watch cannot break through to the trapped families inside.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.4.help: Order the keep's men into the fire
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.4.help.note: The keep's guards pull families from the smoke; three guardsmen die, and the poor quarter's memory of the throne is rewritten.
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.4.pass: Seal the quarter to save the rest
high_kingdom.ev.rescue.4.pass.note: The fire is contained and the city saved; the burned quarter is rebuilt in stone, and the families inside it are not.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.1: A Loan from the Guilds · Saltport
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.1.text: The guilds offer the crown a great loan to meet the winter's costs, at a rate that will make them partners in the treasury for a decade.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.1.deal.note: The winter is paid for and the guilds sit in the counting-house as if born there; every future tax is negotiated with their hand on the scale.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.1.walk.note: You cut the court to the bone and keep the guilds at the door; the treasury is yours, and the winter is very cold.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.2: A Neighbor's Treaty · the Coronation Way
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.2.text: A neighboring realm offers a marriage treaty: your sister for their prince, with a dowry that would settle every debt you have.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.2.deal.note: The treaty is signed and your sister is sent across the border; she writes you dutiful letters that grow shorter every year.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.2.walk.note: You refuse the dowry and keep your sister home; the debts remain, and she never once thanks you for it aloud.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.3: An Enemy's Terms · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.3.text: The Duke offers peace on terms: his son as your heir, or war to the finish of one house or the other.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.3.deal.note: The Duke's boy is raised at your court as your own; the peace holds, and you spend the rest of your life wondering whose hand you are feeding.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.3.walk.note: You choose the war and spend the treasury on it; the realm bleeds, and the histories will call the choice either courage or ruin.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.4.text: A man in the Duke's own household offers to betray his master's plans for a price in land, not gold.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.4.deal: Pay him the land he asks
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.4.deal.note: The betrayer's reports ride south by night; the Duke's every move is known to you, and one day he will find the leak.
high_kingdom.ev.bargain.4.walk.note: You turn him away on principle; half your council calls you a fool, and the other half calls you their king.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.1: The Storm on the March · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.1.text: A blizzard catches you on the road north, and the only light for miles is a crofter's hut with a fire inside.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.1.shelter.no: The crofter gives you his own pallet and sleeps by the door; you learn more about the North in that one night than in a year of councils.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.1.self: Ride on to your own keep
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.1.self.note: You reach the keep frostbitten and proud; two of your escort do not, and the crofter never learns whose door he nearly opened.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.2: A Light in the Wood · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.2.text: Lost in the wood in a night of rain, you see a fire through the trees and hear voices that are not your men.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.2.shelter.no: The fire belongs to deserters from your own levy; they feed you before they recognize you, and the meal is the most honest you eat all year.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.2.self: Turn away and trust your map
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.2.self.note: You find your way out by dawn; the voices remain unidentified, and for years you wonder whether you passed by your own death or your own mercy.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.3.text: The river is up and the ford is drowned, and a ferryman on the far bank asks a price to come across for the king.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.3.shelter.no: He rows you over in the dark and takes your coin without ceremony; on the far bank you realize he never asked your name.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.3.self.note: You make the far bank soaked and shivering, and the ferryman watches you do it; the story of the king who would not pay travels faster than you do.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.4.text: A great storm floods the lower city and cuts the keep off from its own granaries for three days, with the water still rising.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.4.shelter: Open the keep to the flooded
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.4.shelter.no: The keep's halls fill with wet families and their animals; the throne smells of smoke and wet wool for a month, and the city never forgets it.
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.4.self: Keep the keep sealed and dry
high_kingdom.ev.storm_night.4.self.note: The keep stays dry and orderly; the water goes down, and the quarter that drowned its livestock remembers which doors were locked.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.1.text: Old Scholar Alwyn offers you the key to the locked presses of the royal library, where the histories the realm prefers not to teach are kept.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.1.study.note: You spend a winter in the presses and come out knowing exactly which of your ancestors were monsters and which were merely unlucky.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.1.play.note: The key goes back on the ring; you govern by the clean histories, and sleep better for not knowing the difference.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.2.text: A merchant brings you a foreign treatise on the art of governing by consent, which the Church has placed on its list of dangerous books.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.2.study.note: You read it by night and find three ideas you will use for the rest of your reign, and never once admit where they came from.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.2.play.note: The book is burned publicly and you are praised for your piety; the merchant is fined, and the next dangerous book does not come to you.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.3: The Astronomer's Question · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.3.text: An astronomer at the abbey asks the crown's permission to chart the heavens with new instruments, which some clergy call an insult to God.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.3.study.note: The astronomer's charts are strange and accurate; in a generation they will quietly rebuild the realm's calendar and its sense of its own smallness.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.3.play.note: The instruments are put away; the astronomer dies unremarked, and the stars keep their secrets a while longer.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.4: A Tutor for the Heir · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.4.text: A famous teacher offers to educate the heir of the realm, on the condition that the lessons include the failings of the boy's own house.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.4.study.note: The heir learns the truth about his ancestors before he learns to wear the crown; he will be a harder king and a sadder man.
high_kingdom.ev.scholarship.4.play.note: The heir learns the songs and the seals and nothing that would trouble him; he will be a lighter king and an easier one to lie to.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.1: A Field of the Dead · Greenvale
high_kingdom.ev.honor.1.text: After a border skirmish you are offered the honor of the victory, though the fighting was done and the dying suffered by another lord's men.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.1.accept.note: You are praised in the council and in the pulpits; the lord whose men bled hears every word, and says nothing, and does not forget.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.1.decline.note: You give the honor to the man who earned it; the council is startled, and that lord becomes the surest friend you have.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.2: An Enemy's Body · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.honor.2.text: The Duke's own standard-bearer falls in the ford-fight, and the Duke asks for the body back to bury it in the North.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.2.accept.note: The body goes north under escort; the Duke, who expected a trophy, receives a funeral instead, and the war grows one degree cooler.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.2.decline: Keep the banner as a trophy
high_kingdom.ev.honor.2.decline.note: The banner hangs in your hall; the Duke's grief becomes the realm's problem, and the North spends a year making the next battle personal.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.3.text: The daughter of a man hanged for treason asks to be allowed to swear loyalty to the throne, and to keep her father's name if she may.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.3.accept: Let her swear and keep her name
high_kingdom.ev.honor.3.accept.note: She swears, and bears her father's name in your service for thirty years; no one ever again asks whether loyalty runs in blood.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.3.decline: Require her to take a new name
high_kingdom.ev.honor.3.decline.note: She takes the new name and serves you well and coldly; the court calls it mercy, and she calls it a second hanging.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.4: A Broken Oath · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.honor.4.text: A knight of the order has broken a sworn oath to protect a village, and the brothers ask the throne to decide whether he may still be called a knight.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.4.accept.note: He gives up his spurs and wanders; the order is cleansed by one man's ruin, and the village that was not protected is still not protected.
high_kingdom.ev.honor.4.decline: Let the order judge its own
high_kingdom.ev.honor.4.decline.note: The brothers judge him and keep him; the order stands whole and a little less certain of its own name.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.1: The Missing Envoy · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.lost.1.text: An envoy sent to treat with the Holy See has vanished somewhere on the road, along with the letter he carried.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.1.call.note: Your riders find him in a monastery cellar, half-starved and gagged; he had been held by men who wanted the letter, and what he can tell you is worth the search.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.1.wait: Wait and treat by other means
high_kingdom.ev.lost.1.wait.note: You wait; the envoy is never found, and the letter turns up years later in an archive in Rome, exactly where it was always meant to go.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.2.text: A tenant's child has wandered into the wood and not come out, and the parents come to the castle gate because there is nowhere else left to ask.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.2.call: Turn out the household to search
high_kingdom.ev.lost.2.call.note: The wood is beaten all night; the child is found at dawn in a hollow tree, and the household that found her becomes a household that would follow you anywhere.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.2.wait.note: The tenants search for three days and find nothing; the wood gives up a shoe in the spring.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.3: A Lost Standard · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.lost.3.text: The royal standard was lost in the retreat from the ford, and its loss is being read in every tavern as an omen.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.3.call: Offer a reward for its return
high_kingdom.ev.lost.3.call.note: A boy brings it in from a peat bog, mud-caked and unbroken; you pay the reward and have the standard carried before you at the next muster.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.3.wait.note: The new banner flies and the old one stays lost; the taverns note that the realm's honor has been replaced, and priced accordingly.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.4.text: The heir has slipped out of the castle in the night, and no one can say whether he is riding to the border or to a tavern.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.4.call.note: He is found three towns over, drunk and delighted and not at all sorry; you bring him home and say nothing to the court about where he was.
high_kingdom.ev.lost.4.wait: Let him come back on his own
high_kingdom.ev.lost.4.wait.note: He comes back after a week with a taste for the road and a grudge against the walls; the two of you understand each other better and trust each other less.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1: A Dream of the Moor · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1.text: You dream of the first knights breaking their blades on the moor, and in the dream the broken sword is the one you keep above your own hearth.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1.follow: Go to the moor where they broke the blades
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1.follow.note: You ride out to the bare moor and stand where the oath was sworn; you come home and have the old sword brought down and repaired.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1.wake: Ignore the dream and burn the impulse
high_kingdom.ev.dream.1.wake.note: The dream fades; the broken sword stays above the hearth, and you find yourself glancing at it less and less.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.2: A Dream of the Dead King · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.dream.2.text: In the dream your dead father sits on the throne and will not speak to you, only points at the door through which he once entered.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.2.follow.note: You dream yourself through it and wake not knowing what you saw, only that your first order that morning is one you had spent a year avoiding.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.2.wake.note: You wake sweating and swear off dreams; the door in your life stays unopened, and your father stays silent for the rest of your reign.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.3: A Dream of a Field of Wheat · Greenvale
high_kingdom.ev.dream.3.text: You dream of a field of wheat with no one to reap it, stretching to the horizon, and wake certain it means something.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.3.follow: Ride to the valley and look
high_kingdom.ev.dream.3.follow.note: There is no hidden field, but you spend three days walking the farms and return with a plan for the grain reserves that feeds the realm in the next bad year.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.3.wake.note: You go about your duties; the fields of Greenvale fail that autumn, and you remember the dream at a very bad moment.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.4: A Dream of the White Tower · the Capital
high_kingdom.ev.dream.4.text: You dream the White Tower is on fire, and above it, unharmed, hangs the Iron Crown in mid-air.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.4.follow.note: You warn the abbess to check the abbey's lamps; one is found to be cracked in the crypt, and no one ever learns why the king sent word.
high_kingdom.ev.dream.4.wake.note: You laugh, and say nothing; the abbey's lamp cracks on its own and takes a storeroom. The dream is filed away with all the others.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.1: A Wager at the Muster · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.bet.1.text: At the muster, Lord Reginald wagers a chest of silver that his man will unhorse yours in the lists.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.1.match.note: Your man wins by a hair; Reginald pays with a smile, and the two of you have now made a public spectacle worth more to him than silver.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.1.fold.note: You leave the wager on the table; your man wins anyway, and the hall notices that you would not stake a thing on your own.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.2.text: A young lord has lost everything at Saltport's tables, including lands he holds of you, and asks you to cover his debt before the harbor-men take him apart.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.2.match.note: You settle the account and take a lien on the lands; the young lord is grateful, and the harbor knows the throne's credit is good.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.2.fold.note: He is beaten in an alley and loses the lands anyway to the guilds, who now sit on your southwestern border.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.3: A Wager on the Succession · the Lords' Council
high_kingdom.ev.bet.3.text: At the council table, older lords are openly taking wagers on how long the old king has left, and one of them asks you for a stake.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.3.match: Answer the wager with a larger one
high_kingdom.ev.bet.3.match.note: You bet openly against the oldest lord; the table laughs and the question of the succession, for one evening, becomes a joke instead of a knife.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.3.fold.note: You forbid wagers on the king's death; the talk stops in public, and the wagers move to a back room where you can no longer hear them.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.4: A Dicing Debt of Your Own · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.bet.4.text: Half-drunk after the feast, you have lost a sum at dice that the treasury cannot quietly cover.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.4.match: Play on and win it back
high_kingdom.ev.bet.4.match.note: You win it back and then some, and the court discovers that its king is lucky — which is a dangerous thing for a court to know.
high_kingdom.ev.bet.4.fold.note: You stop, and pay the debt from your own purse, and let the court see the fool as well as the king.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.1: The Hermit of the Wood · the Knights' Wood
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.1.text: A holy hermit lives in the order's wood, and the knights say he was once a lord who gave away everything after a war he won.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.1.learn.note: You sit two hours and he talks of the war he won; you go home and change one policy and sleep worse and rule better.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.1.mock.note: You ride past his hut and say loud, cheerful things; the knights hear you, and the hermit says nothing, and neither do they.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.2: A Madman in the Crypt · the White Tower
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.2.text: A ragged man in the crypt of the White Tower claims to be a prophet and tells every visitor exactly how the realm will end.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.2.learn: Ask him to say it plainly
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.2.learn.note: He says it plainly, and it is close enough to your own private fears that you have him fed and watched and never mention the conversation to anyone.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.2.mock.note: He is whipped from the churchyard; within a year his prophecy is being repeated with your name inserted, by people who never met him.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.3: A Fool at the Gate · Ironhold
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.3.text: A wandering fool appears at the gate and offers, for a coin, to tell the king the one true thing he knows.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.3.learn.note: He leans in and tells you the one true thing; you never repeat it, and for the rest of your life you catch yourself checking whether it was right.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.3.mock.note: He is whipped from the gate; years later, in the mouth of a man you trusted, you hear the same sentence again, and no one can tell you where he got it.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.4: A Monk Who Left the World · the Northern March
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.4.text: A monk in the March has abandoned the order to live alone in a cave, and the Church asks you to bring him back.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.4.learn: Go alone and hear him out
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.4.learn.note: You climb to the cave and hear why he left; what he says about the realm from that distance stays with you longer than any sermon.
high_kingdom.ev.hermit.4.mock.note: The soldiers bring him back down; he is returned to the order, and he never speaks another word to anyone.
high_kingdom.ev.quiet.text: No herald, no petition, no knife in the dark: for one hour the realm leaves you alone, and the fire does the talking.
high_kingdom.ev.omen.text: A red star burns over Ironhold for three nights, and the court's astronomers and its priests spend the time arguing about whose jurisdiction the sky is.
high_kingdom.ev.hard.text: Bad news, thin coffers, and a cold that will not break: the realm endures, the way it always has, one grudging day at a time.
high_kingdom.ev.dread.text: Nothing has happened — and that is the trouble. Every corridor is quiet, and quiet is where the knife is being sharpened.
high_kingdom.ev.bounty.text: Full barns, fat herds, and a mild season: for once the realm has more than it can spend, and everyone is briefly, warily kind.
high_kingdom.ev.weariness.text: You have signed so many names onto so many fates that yours has begun to feel like one more seal at the foot of a page.
high_kingdom.beh.care.1: Unbuckles your armor and tends your wounds
high_kingdom.beh.care.1.res: Someone dressed your hurts by the fire.
high_kingdom.beh.care.2: Sends for the royal physician to take your pulse
high_kingdom.beh.care.2.res: The physician saw to you with care.
high_kingdom.beh.care.3: Sits by your sickbed the whole night
high_kingdom.beh.care.3.res: Someone watched over your bedside till dawn.
high_kingdom.beh.meal.1: Brings a dish of hot broth
high_kingdom.beh.meal.1.res: A bowl of broth warmed you to the bone.
high_kingdom.beh.meal.2: Leaves a basket of autumn fruit
high_kingdom.beh.meal.3: Asks you to sup at his table
high_kingdom.beh.meal.3.res: A supper eaten without a knife at your back.
high_kingdom.beh.coin.1: Presses a purse of silver into your hand
high_kingdom.beh.coin.2.res: Someone cleared an old account for you.
high_kingdom.beh.coin.3.res: A weight of gold eased your need.
high_kingdom.beh.talk.2: Argues the state of the realm with you
high_kingdom.beh.talk.2.res: The argument showed you which way the wind blew.
high_kingdom.beh.talk.3.res: After the long talk you were not alone.
high_kingdom.beh.teach.1.res: You learned a new stroke of the blade.
high_kingdom.beh.teach.2: Walks you through a battle formation
high_kingdom.beh.teach.2.res: You glimpsed the logic of the shield-wall.
high_kingdom.beh.teach.3: Passes on the art of serving a king
high_kingdom.beh.teach.3.res: You kept a lesson good for a lifetime.
high_kingdom.beh.train.1: Hauls weapons and armor beside you
high_kingdom.beh.train.2: Rides out with you at a gallop
high_kingdom.beh.train.2.res: You steadied yourself in the saddle.
high_kingdom.beh.train.3: Teaches you to stand steady in full plate
high_kingdom.beh.train.3.res: You learned to bear the weight and walk.
high_kingdom.beh.warn.1.res: You stepped clear of the gossip in time.
high_kingdom.beh.warn.2: Warns you to watch your own courtiers
high_kingdom.beh.warn.2.res: You grew warier of those close to you.
high_kingdom.beh.warn.3: Urges you not to cross the throne
high_kingdom.beh.gift.1.res: You received a token to keep.
high_kingdom.beh.gift.2.res: A good horse steadied your road.
high_kingdom.beh.gift.3: Gives you a family book of arms
high_kingdom.beh.gift.3.res: An old volume lit your desk.
high_kingdom.beh.song.2.res: The tune carried you to far country.
high_kingdom.beh.rest.1: Lets you doze against his shoulder
